The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

4 5 ## Introduction 6 7 Brotli is a generic-purpose lossless compression algorithm that compresses data 8 using a combination of a modern variant of the LZ77 algorithm, Huffman coding 9 and 2nd order context modeling, with a compression ratio comparable to the best 10 currently available general-purpose compression methods. It is similar in speed 11 with deflate but offers more dense compression. 12 13 The specification of the Brotli Compressed Data Format is defined in 14 [RFC 7932](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7932). 15 16 Brotli is open-sourced under the MIT License, see the LICENSE file. 17 18 > **Please note:** brotli is a "stream" format; it does not contain 19 > meta-information, like checksums or uncompressed data length. It is possible 20 > to modify "raw" ranges of the compressed stream and the decoder will not 21 > notice that. 22 23 ## Command-Line Tool 24 25 The `brotli` command-line tool can compress and decompress files. 26 27 ### Basic Usage 28 29 Compress a file: 30 ``` 31 brotli input.txt 32 ``` 33 34 Decompress a file: 35 ``` 36 brotli --decompress input.txt.br 37 ``` 38 39 Compress to stdout: 40 ``` 41 brotli --stdout input.txt > output.br 42 ``` 43 44 Decompress from stdin: 45 ``` 46 cat input.txt.br | brotli --decompress --stdout 47 ``` 48 49 ### Command Aliases 50 51 - `brcat` is equivalent to `brotli --decompress --concatenated --stdout` 52 - `unbrotli` is equivalent to `brotli --decompress` 53 54 ### Common Options 55 56 - `-#` or `--quality=#`: Set compression quality (0-11, default: 11) 57 - `-d` or `--decompress`: Decompress mode 58 - `-c` or `--stdout`: Write to stdout 59 - `-f` or `--force`: Overwrite existing output files 60 - `-k` or `--keep`: Keep input files (default behavior) 61 - `--rm`: Remove input files after processing 62 - `-t` or `--test`: Test compressed file integrity 63 - `-v` or `--verbose`: Verbose output 64 - `-h` or `--help`: Display help information 65 - `-V` or `--version`: Display version information 66 67 ### Operation Modes 68 69 1. **Compression mode** (default): Compress input files 70 2. **Decompression mode** (`--decompress`): Decompress input files 71 3. **Test mode** (`--test`): Verify integrity of compressed files 72 73 ### Examples 74 75 Compress with specific quality level: 76 ``` 77 brotli -q 9 input.txt 78 ``` 79 80 Decompress multiple files: 81 ``` 82 brotli -d file1.br file2.br file3.br 83 ``` 84 85 Compress and remove original: 86 ``` 87 brotli --rm input.txt 88 ``` 89 90 Test compressed file: 91 ``` 92 brotli --test file.br 93 ``` 94 95 For more detailed information, see the brotli(1) manual page.
